executive_summary: The supplied files show several validation risks. The most severe observed issue is a future-oracle economic backtest in the strong contrarian pipeline: execution uses sweep labels and first-hit timing that are only knowable after the signal time. The squeeze signal backtest is also materially weaker than the full-stream backtest because it operates on walk-forward prediction rows rather than every chronological snapshot, and its reported event_rate is 1.0 for top configurations. Model reports show strong dependence on symbol/calendar features, weak incremental topology value for the 1h direction task, heavy grid search over the same OOS folds, overlapping time-series observations, missing calibration evidence, and misleading ranking where selected configurations can have negative net expectancy. Some safeguards are present, including chronological splits, stated embargoes, and explicit forbidden feature patterns, but row-level evidence proving event-level purge, no duplicate-event overlap, calibration stability, and symbol/timeframe generalization is missing.

findings.title: Strong contrarian economic backtest uses future sweep labels as an execution oracle

evidence.detail: simulate_candidate reads candidate.sweep_code_1h and candidate.first_hit_seconds_1h, rejects candidates unless the farther side was swept first, then derives expected_hit_time_ns from first_hit_seconds_1h before selecting the entry snapshot.
sweep_code_1h and first_hit_seconds_1h are built by inspecting future prices inside (logged_at, logged_at + horizon].
The backtest merges feature rows with SWEEP_LABEL_PATH and passes sweep_code_1h and first_hit_seconds_1h into trade simulation.

findings.why_it_matters: A live strategy cannot know at signal time whether the farther liquidity side will be swept first or the future first-hit timestamp. Using these labels for entry selection and timing can turn a label/outcome study into a look-ahead backtest.
findings.verification_test: Run an ablation backtest that removes sweep_code_1h and first_hit_seconds_1h from execution-time decision logic. Signals may be selected only from model probability and features available at logged_at; entries must be generated by a causal stop/limit rule observed in the future price stream without pre-filtering on future sweep labels.
findings.recommended_change: Separate label/outcome construction from tradable execution. Treat sweep_code_1h and first_hit_seconds_1h as target/outcome fields only, never as signal filters or entry-time inputs. Implement a causal order simulation where the strategy places orders at logged_at and the simulator later determines fills.
findings.success_metric: A static check confirms zero references to sweep_code_1h, first_hit_seconds_1h, post_hit_continuation_pct_1h, or strong_contrarian_* labels in signal selection and entry timing code. The causal backtest report must include signal_count, fill_count, precision, and net metrics computed without label columns in the execution path.
findings.risk: Reported economic performance for this strategy may be materially invalid until the oracle fields are removed from execution.

findings.title: Squeeze signal backtest is event-conditioned and reports event_rate of 1.0

evidence.detail: load_data reads PREDICTIONS_PATH from walk_forward_predictions.parquet and merges those prediction rows with features; it does not score every 1h topology snapshot.
Best configuration has event_rate = 1.0 and event_direction_accuracy = 0.9852941176470589; many top configurations also show event_rate = 1.0.
The separate full-stream report states every chronological 1h topology snapshot in each test fold is scored and reports 547327 full_stream_rows and 246435 oos_scored_rows.

findings.why_it_matters: If the signal backtest only evaluates rows already belonging to an event-oriented prediction dataset, precision and direction accuracy can be conditioned on the presence of an event and will not estimate alert quality on the full stream.
findings.verification_test: Compare the set of ids in topology_v2_squeeze_signal generated_signals against the full 1h feature stream for the same fold windows. Measure the base event rate of the prediction input before thresholding and confirm whether non-event snapshots are represented at their natural frequency.
findings.recommended_change: Use the full-stream scoring pipeline for alert evaluation and treat the squeeze_signal report as event-row diagnostics unless proven otherwise. Require all production-like alert metrics to be computed over every chronological 1h snapshot in each test fold.
findings.success_metric: For each fold, input coverage equals the count of 1h feature rows in the fold window, and pre-threshold event_rate is reported. Alert event_precision must be computed as detected_events_within_window / all_alerts, not only on event-conditioned rows.
findings.risk: Event precision and event_direction_accuracy in the signal backtest can be overstated and not comparable to live alert rates.

findings.title: No observed event-level group purge preventing the same liquidity event from contributing to train, validation, and test

evidence.detail: load_event_training_data requires id, logged_at, symbol, target_event, and model features; no event_id or event_time grouping field is required for purging duplicate precursor rows of the same event.

historical event data for each fold is selected by logged_at < test_start - EMBARGO, where EMBARGO is 1 hour. The script splits historical rows into train and validation using logged_at quantiles plus a 1 hour embargo.
Methodology states event_window_minutes = 60.0 and each fold is retrained using historical event-dataset rows, but the report does not show event-level group purge counts.

findings.why_it_matters: Multiple precursor snapshots can describe the same future liquidity event. Row-level time embargo can still permit near-duplicate event representations across train/validation/test if event windows straddle boundaries or if events have multiple precursor rows.
findings.verification_test: Attach a stable event key to every event-dataset row, such as symbol plus actual_event_time/event_name/direction, then compute intersections of event keys between train, validation, and test for each fold after purge. Also count rows whose label window overlaps any validation or test interval.
findings.recommended_change: Use purged group time-series validation. Remove all training rows whose label window overlaps validation/test windows and all rows sharing the same event key with validation/test events. Store fold purge statistics in the report.
findings.success_metric: For every fold: train_event_keys ∩ validation_event_keys = 0, train_event_keys ∩ test_event_keys = 0, and no training label window intersects validation/test time ranges. Report purged row counts and remaining class counts.
findings.risk: Model validation may benefit from seeing near-duplicate representations of the same liquidation event in historical folds.

findings.title: Large OOS grid search reuses the same folds without an observed nested final holdout

evidence.detail: Grid contains 48 alert configurations, 162 execution configurations, and 7776 total backtests; best_configuration is selected from the same report.
Grid also contains 7776 total backtests and reports top_20 selected from the same folds.
The script sorts summary by research_score, positive_folds, mean_net_bps, and profit_factor, then writes top configurations. No nested untouched holdout split is shown in the supplied code.

findings.why_it_matters: Selecting the best configuration from thousands of trials on the same OOS folds creates multiple-comparison and data-snooping risk. Fold metrics become model-selection metrics rather than unbiased final estimates.
findings.verification_test: Freeze the selected configuration using only training/validation folds, then evaluate exactly once on a later untouched chronological holdout that was not used for model training, threshold selection, grid search, or research_score design.
findings.recommended_change: Introduce nested walk-forward validation: inner validation for thresholds and grid selection, outer chronological holdout for final reporting. Report all tried configurations and the selection rule before outer evaluation.
findings.success_metric: The final report contains an untouched outer holdout period, exactly one pre-registered selected configuration evaluated on it, and a trial-adjusted summary such as bootstrap or permutation confidence intervals across folds/events.
findings.risk: The reported best configuration may be a selection artifact even when individual fold scoring is chronological.

findings.title: 1h direction models are dominated by symbol/calendar effects, with weak incremental topology value

evidence.detail: calendar_only test balanced_accuracy = 0.4501181944262669; topology_only test balanced_accuracy = 0.4038438389491346; combined test balanced_accuracy = 0.44096298934188555; combined_gain_vs_calendar = -0.009155205084381335.
CatBoost top features include symbol, dow_sin, hour_sin, hour_cos, is_weekend_utc, and dow_cos before most topology features.

findings.why_it_matters: A model driven by symbol and calendar may not be learning transferable liquidation topology. It can degrade when symbol mix, exchange regime, or time-of-week effects shift.
findings.verification_test: Run leave-one-symbol-out and leave-one-timeframe-out validation. Also train with symbol and calendar features removed and compare balanced_accuracy, macro_f1, log_loss, and calibration by symbol/timeframe.
findings.recommended_change: Report topology-only, calendar-only, symbol-blind, and group-held-out performance as first-class validation results. Treat topology claims as unsupported unless topology features improve group-held-out metrics beyond calendar baselines.
findings.success_metric: On held-out symbols/timeframes, topology-enabled models improve balanced_accuracy and log_loss versus calendar-only by a pre-registered margin, and no single symbol/timeframe contributes more than a pre-specified share of total lift.
findings.risk: Claims about topology signal may actually reflect non-stationary calendar or symbol effects.

findings.title: Dense overlapping time-series rows inflate apparent sample size

evidence.detail: Dataset spans 2026-03-30 to 2026-08-05 with 2554739 valid_labeled_rows; reported sample_rows are 800000 train, 300000 validation, and 300000 test.
Every row receives forward labels for 15m, 1h, and 4h using future prices. There is no non-overlapping sampling step in label construction.
This separate matrix study explicitly implements non_overlapping_sample for t-statistics, but analogous non-overlap reporting is not shown in the supplied model metric reports.

findings.why_it_matters: Adjacent snapshots share most features and overlapping forward-return windows. Treating hundreds of thousands of rows as independent can understate uncertainty and produce unstable confidence estimates.
findings.verification_test: Recompute validation/test metrics using one observation per symbol/timeframe per horizon bucket, and separately using block bootstrap by day or by detected event. Compare point estimates and confidence intervals with row-level metrics.
findings.recommended_change: Add non-overlapping and block-bootstrap metrics to every report. Use event-level or time-block effective sample sizes when ranking configurations.
findings.success_metric: Reports include row_count, non_overlapping_count, effective_sample_size estimate, and 95% block-bootstrap intervals for balanced_accuracy, precision, PR-AUC, mean_net_bps, and profit_factor.
findings.risk: Validation metrics may appear more stable than they are.

findings.title: Research-score ranking can select configurations with negative or near-zero net expectancy

evidence.detail: Best configuration has mean_net_bps = -3.3333093933307953, median_net_bps = -15.004219142807239, total_net_bps = -239.99827631981725, and profit_factor = 0.79241506507768, yet research_score = 7.4956690190556.
Best configuration has mean_net_bps = -0.0495200280758433, total_net_bps = -3.3673619091573443, and profit_factor = 0.9955974240039208, yet research_score = 24.39951986297695.
calculate_research_score includes positive weights for event_rate, direction_accuracy, win_rate, fold_ratio, and capped profit_factor even when mean_net_bps is negative.

findings.why_it_matters: A ranking function that rewards event diagnostics despite negative net returns can make a losing configuration appear best. This is especially dangerous when users interpret research_score as strategy quality.
findings.verification_test: Re-rank all configurations using only pre-registered economic and validation-safe metrics after costs, with constraints on minimum fold performance. Compare selected configurations and their outer-holdout results.
findings.recommended_change: Separate classification diagnostics from economic selection. Require mean_net_bps, median_net_bps, profit_factor, and fold consistency constraints before computing any composite score.
findings.success_metric: No configuration with mean_net_bps <= 0, profit_factor <= 1, or fewer than a pre-specified number of positive folds can be selected as best. Reports must display the reason for rejection for ineligible configurations.
findings.risk: Misleading model-selection incentives can promote configurations that do not survive costs.

findings.title: Strong contrarian classification is highly imbalanced and precision remains low at selected thresholds

evidence.detail: Target positive_rate = 0.08323730847234463.
Full_combined test validation_selected_threshold has precision = 0.13908739937571873, recall = 0.38862749598347485, and f1 = 0.20485754037868248.
Full_combined test_pr_auc = 0.1280341788404858 while selected threshold precision = 0.13908739937571873.

findings.why_it_matters: ROC-AUC and lift can look acceptable under class imbalance while precision remains low. Low precision can produce many false positives and unstable downstream backtests.
findings.verification_test: Report precision-recall curves, base-rate-normalized lift, expected false positives per day, and calibration by probability bucket for each fold and group. Evaluate thresholds chosen only on validation against test precision stability.
findings.recommended_change: Use PR-AUC, precision at fixed alert rate, and calibrated probability thresholds as primary metrics for rare-event models. Include fold and symbol/timeframe precision tables.
findings.success_metric: For each fold and major symbol/timeframe group, selected thresholds meet pre-registered minimum precision and minimum sample-count requirements; confidence intervals for precision exclude the base rate by the required margin.
findings.risk: Rare-event performance can be overstated if selection relies on ROC-AUC or lift without precision stability.

findings.title: Calibration and confidence-bucket stability are not demonstrated

evidence.detail: The diagnostic script can create probability_profile.csv and confidence_performance.csv, but those output files are not included in the supplied project files.

Distance_only top_fraction_metrics are non-monotonic: top_1pct_event_rate = 0.07133333333333333, top_2pct_event_rate = 0.07883333333333334, top_5pct_event_rate = 0.07546666666666667, top_10pct_event_rate = 0.0891.

Top 12 configurations with minimum_direction_confidence from 0.55 to 0.70 have identical alerts, event_precision, direction_accuracy, and trade metrics, indicating confidence thresholds are not differentiating those selected signals.

findings.why_it_matters: Uncalibrated probabilities and unstable confidence buckets make percentile thresholds, alert rates, and direction confidence filters unreliable. Identical outcomes across confidence thresholds can hide ineffective filtering.
findings.verification_test: Compute calibration curves, expected calibration error, Brier score, and bucketed event rates for every fold, symbol, timeframe, and confidence decile. Check monotonicity of event rate by predicted probability and direction_confidence bucket.
findings.recommended_change: Add probability calibration reporting and, if needed, fit calibration only on validation folds. Use bucket-level minimum sample counts and confidence intervals before deploying percentile thresholds.
findings.success_metric: Each reported model includes ECE, Brier score, log_loss, and bucket tables. High-confidence buckets must show statistically higher event rates than lower buckets on validation and test, with no fold having fewer than the minimum bucket sample count.
findings.risk: Thresholds and confidence filters may be unstable, producing alert rates that do not transfer.

findings.title: Future-derived label columns are retained in labeled parquet and require strict feature guards

evidence.detail: The output parquet retains future_time_*, future_price_*, future_delay_seconds_*, forward_return_*, direction_*, and label_valid_* columns; only target_time_* columns are dropped.
forbidden_patterns include future_, forward_return_, direction_, label_valid_, and target_time_. The listed model features exclude these columns.
The CatBoost feature list shown in metrics excludes future_, forward_return_, direction_, label_valid_, and target_time_ columns.

findings.why_it_matters: The supplied baseline and CatBoost feature lists appear to exclude future-derived columns, but retaining those columns in the modeling parquet creates a latent leakage risk for any future script that auto-selects columns.
findings.verification_test: Add a CI test that loads every training script's feature list and fails if any selected feature matches forbidden_patterns or if target-derived columns are present in model input matrices.
findings.recommended_change: Write separate feature-only and label-only artifacts, or enforce a central feature registry that explicitly whitelists allowed columns. Make forbidden-pattern checks mandatory before every model fit.
findings.success_metric: Automated leakage tests pass for all model training scripts, and logged training matrices contain zero columns matching future_, forward_return_, direction_, label_valid_, target_time_, sweep_code_*, first_hit_seconds_*, or strong_contrarian_* except as target fields.
findings.risk: A future experiment can accidentally train on labels or future prices even if the current supplied models did not.

findings.title: Top configurations contain many exact duplicate outcomes, indicating ineffective grid dimensions

evidence.detail: Configs 3934 through 5394 vary minimum_direction_confidence and minimum_target_distance_bps but have identical alerts = 72, event_precision = 0.6944444444444444, direction_accuracy = 0.92, mean_net_bps = -3.3333093933307953, and research_score = 7.4956690190556.

Multiple top configurations varying minimum_direction_confidence and minimum_target_distance_bps have identical raw_signals, trades, win_rate, mean_net_bps, profit_factor, event_rate, and research_score.

findings.why_it_matters: Duplicate results reduce the effective search diversity and can give a false impression of robust top-ranked configurations. They also suggest some hyperparameters are not active for the selected signal set.
findings.verification_test: Hash each configuration's selected signal ids and trade ids. Count unique signal/trade sets among top configurations and across the full grid. Identify parameters that do not change selections.
findings.recommended_change: Deduplicate configurations by resulting signal/trade set before ranking. Remove or narrow inactive grid dimensions unless they materially change signals or execution.
findings.success_metric: Top-N reports include unique_signal_set_count and unique_trade_set_count. No more than a pre-specified fraction of the top configurations may be exact duplicates unless explicitly labeled as parameter-equivalent.
findings.risk: Robustness may be overstated by repeated copies of the same trades.

findings.title: Symbol/timeframe group stability is reported for one walk-forward model but not consistently used as a selection gate

evidence.detail: Group metrics show substantial variation by symbol and symbol_timeframe; for example, fold_3 XAUUSDT base_rate = 0.01439292690449265 and top_1pct_event_rate = 0.08247422680412371, while SOLUSDT base rates and lifts differ materially.
Fold test_base_rate changes from 0.102016 to 0.090364 to 0.05796 across folds; test_pr_auc changes from 0.18831844762197553 to 0.17270403242155483 to 0.1270296595410882.
The top-level best_configuration reports positive_folds and fold_count but does not include symbol/timeframe minimum performance gates.

findings.why_it_matters: A strategy can look acceptable in aggregate while being concentrated in specific symbols, timeframes, or regimes. Without group gates, symbol/timeframe dependence can become hidden deployment risk.
findings.verification_test: For every selected configuration, compute fold-by-symbol, fold-by-timeframe, and fold-by-symbol_timeframe metrics including event rate, precision, net_bps, profit_factor, and alert count. Re-rank after requiring minimum sample sizes and non-degenerate performance in each major group.
findings.recommended_change: Use group-aware selection gates or explicitly mark unsupported groups. Report aggregate metrics only alongside group dispersion and worst-group metrics.
findings.success_metric: Selected configurations pass pre-registered minimum row/trade counts and minimum validation metrics for each supported symbol/timeframe group, or the report clearly excludes unsupported groups from deployment scope.
findings.risk: Aggregate validation may hide dependence on a small number of favorable symbol/timeframe regimes.

missing_evidence: Row-level parquet contents for squeeze_event_dataset.parquet, detected_squeeze_events.parquet, walk_forward_predictions.parquet, full_stream_oos_scores.parquet, generated_signals.parquet, all_trades.parquet, and fold_metrics.csv were not supplied.
The source script scripts/research_topology_v2_squeeze_events.py was referenced but not supplied, so event-dataset construction, precursor-row generation, and event-key availability are unknown.
No row-level event_id or stable liquidity-event key was supplied to prove that the same event cannot appear across train, validation, and test.
No calibration reports, reliability diagrams, expected calibration error, Brier scores, or confidence bucket output files were supplied.
No leave-one-symbol-out, leave-one-timeframe-out, or symbol-blind validation reports were supplied for the main squeeze and direction models.
No nested final chronological holdout report was supplied after grid selection.
No CI or automated leakage-test output was supplied showing that forbidden future-derived columns are blocked for every training script.
No raw feature-generation provenance was supplied for data/features/liq_topology_v2.parquet, so upstream availability timing of nearest liquidity features is unknown.
top_3_next_actions: Fix the strong contrarian economic backtest by removing sweep_code_1h and first_hit_seconds_1h from all signal and execution decisions; rerun as a causal order simulation.
Add event-level purged walk-forward validation with stable event keys, non-overlapping/block-bootstrap metrics, and an untouched outer holdout for all grid-selected configurations.

Create a mandatory leakage and calibration report for every model: forbidden-column check, feature availability audit, reliability buckets, ECE/Brier/log_loss, and group metrics by fold/symbol/timeframe.
